title: Scorer Reliability Toolkit: Comparing LLM Judges Against Human Annotations on Safety Datasets
original_idea: Build a Python script that takes a sample of safety-labeled prompts and responses, runs multiple LLM judges, and computes inter-rater reliability metrics (Cohen's kappa, Fleiss' kappa, confusion matrices). Validate on a subset of the AILuminate public dataset.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Judge reliability directly affects the trustworthiness of all safety evaluations. A diagnostic tool addresses a foundational methodological concern.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Python scripting, API calls to LLM judges, computing kappa statistics. Well within CS student skills. Standard libraries available.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Build one tool, validate on one dataset. Clear deliverable. Scope is well-contained.

novelty.reasoning: Judge's Verdict Benchmark (2025-2026) already systematically evaluates 54 LLMs as judges using Cohen's Kappa, finding top models achieve kappa 0.781-0.816. Research on multilingual LLM judge reliability (EMNLP 2025 Findings) measures cross-dataset consistency. CMU's work on rating indeterminacy in LLM-as-a-Judge systems (Dec 2025) addresses validation challenges. The proposed Python script computing kappa statistics across LLM judges on safety data closely mirrors the Judge's Verdict methodology. The specific focus on safety datasets (AILuminate) adds a modest narrowing, but the methodological contribution is well-covered.
